A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian CT reconstruction work, with matching authors, method components and benchmark results despite renaming GRCT to DGR. All supplied pages are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–F, which were also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on AAPM-Mayo LDCT and FUMPE, together with computational measurements and box-size and acceleration ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original clinical-data reconstruction results and adds DGR results on FIPS, loss-function ablations and qualitative reconstruction analyses.

M1.justification: The Gaussian representation, local confinement, discretization and parallel accumulation remain. The stated reconstruction objective changes from squared L2 loss in v1 Equation 21 to L1 loss in v2 Equation 13. Appendix D adds weighted SSIM/TV loss variants, while the projection formulation is generalized from a specified Radon matrix to a geometry-dependent operator.

E1.justification: v2 adds real measured cone-beam reconstruction on FIPS walnut, pine and seashell cases at 75, 50 and 25 views. This substantially extends the represented objects, acquisition geometry and measurement conditions beyond the retained AAPM-Mayo and FUMPE clinical-image experiments.

E2.justification: NeRP and generic 3DGS are removed from all six retained clinical benchmark comparisons. The new FIPS comparison includes FDK, IntraTomo, NAF, SAX-NeRF, X-Gaussian and R2-Gaussian at two iteration budgets. v2 states that X-Gaussian was evaluated using official code, while the other baseline results were taken from R2-Gaussian.

E3.justification: The stated 4-view and 8-view training budgets decrease from 2K and 3K iterations to 1K each. Standard fan-beam SVCT changes from a fixed 30K budget to stopping when projection-space validation loss converges. New FIPS comparisons report 300- and 1,000-iteration DGR settings, and the loss ablations use 300 iterations. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D newly reports loss-component ablations across cone-beam SVCT, fan-beam SVCT and LACT. Appendix F adds reconstruction trajectories, an 8-view bone-structure comparison with DiffusionMBIR and Gaussian spatial visualizations. The original box-size and acceleration ablations remain; the initialization trajectories concern different tasks rather than a controlled initialization comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Appendix C's explanation of averaging metrics across slices clarifies evaluation aggregation rather than introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds FIPS quality/time results, loss-ablation scores and qualitative findings; for example, Table 1 reports 41.28 PSNR and 0.952 SSIM for 75-view DGR at 1,000 iterations. NeRP/3DGS result rows and v1 Figure 4's comparative runtime measurements disappear. Retained clinical benchmark scores and the original two ablation tables remain numerically identical despite revised stated settings, so they do not demonstrate a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: v2 replaces explicit Radon-integral and sparse/limited-angle sampling formulations with a regularized inverse-problem formulation and adds asymptotic complexity analysis in Appendix E.2. Its main-text quadratic expansion corrects v1's positive cross terms to negative terms, consistent with B'' = B' - delta_mu. However, Algorithm 1 retains the old positive signs, and the new decomposed complexity claim omits Gaussian-count dependence without justification.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain direct Gaussian volume reconstruction and efficient parallel aggregation without supervised neural-network training. v2 more explicitly distinguishes DGR from adaptations of 3DGS, extends its stated experimental claims to real cone-beam reconstruction, and adds introduction-level claims of plausible results within five minutes and convergence around fifteen minutes.

C2.justification: v2 adds the explanation that learnable Gaussian intensities can compensate for excluded distant contributions, and motivates SSIM and TV losses through projection structure and volume sparsity. It removes v1's explicit discussion of severe-view performance degradation and stability across anatomical planes. The principal interpretations of box-size and view-count effects remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents FBP-based Gaussian initialization, ODL projection synthesis, metric aggregation, loss weights and scatter-add volume assembly in Algorithm 1. Hardware changes from an A40 to an RTX 6000 for most experiments and an RTX 3090 for FIPS. Code disclosure changes from a planned release to reported review attachments with reproduction instructions; attachment availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially rebuilt around DLR and reconstruction-based methods. Newly discussed work includes IntraTomo, NAF, SAX-NeRF, 3DGR-CAR, DIF-Gaussian, X-Gaussian and R2-Gaussian. v2 positions DGR against CT-specific Gaussian approaches and density voxelization, while removing the NeRP citation and several earlier references.

P1.justification: The title and GRCT terminology change to DGR, while the abstract, introduction, background and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Numbered sections replace unnumbered headings, experiments are reorganized around acquisition geometry, and Appendices A–F provide a new explanatory structure. This exceeds simple expansion through added experiments.

P2.justification: v1's runtime bar chart is removed. v2 adds the FIPS comparison table, three loss-ablation tables, reconstruction and 3D visualizations in Figures 4–7, and Algorithm 1. Existing tables lose comparator rows and are rearranged; Figures 1–2 receive revised labels and captions. Figure 3 retains the original reconstruction comparison.

improvement.justification: The measured FIPS benchmark, CT-specific comparisons, loss ablations and implementation details strengthen the evidence and make v2 easier to audit. However, its claim of best PSNR at every FIPS view count contradicts Table 1: at 25 views, IntraTomo scores 35.85 versus DGR's 35.16/34.58. Conflicting main-text/pseudocode signs and the unjustified Gaussian-count-independent complexity bound further limit the benefits. The broader evidence and documentation support a limited net improvement.
